item.title: Downvote
item.content:encoded:
Well, this is just sad. For me, this article fails because it tries to be a joke. Someone previously said that SCPs can be funny, but we need to establish a limit here. When an article has a joke in it, that's fine, but when your whole article tries to be a joke, then it can only be a -J.

It's a random message that kills people, and the message is still in the article for everyone to read anyway? In universe it should be censored, but that would kill the punchline, and here we have the problem again: the whole article is a joke, so without the punchline it becomes pointless. Come on, at least create a narrative to keep the reader engaged until the secret killer funny message is revealed or anything like that. There is no story, no interesting anomaly, there is nothing good here, really.

I think we all need to remember that joke SCPs are separate from the main list for a reason. - 1.

item.title: SCP Concept - The Drain Cover
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror

Page Layout (Optional): N/A (Suggestions Needed)

Elevator Pitch:

  • A floor drain cover that constantly emits a gurgling sound typical in a drain clogged with semi-permeable debris.
  • Upon inspection, it will begin to overflow and fill the room with dark, murky water until the victim drowns.
  • The water overflowing from the drain cover is chemically identical, but significantly less dense than normal water. This makes it very difficult to swim or float in.
  • The drain cover will only begin to overflow if the room is small and closed.
  • All effects only occur when the drain cover is appropriately fixed over a floor drain.

Central Narrative: None (yet)

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The theme is the fear of drowning and the disgust of a drain overflowing with dirty water.

Additional Notes:

  • I want the drain cover to have some psychological abilities, such as:
      • Making victims believe all exits are locked or otherwise broken.
      • Making victims believe the water is unbearably cold.
      • Causing uncontrollable panic when the overflowing begins.

All feedback and criticism is wanted. I am very new to the site and have been thinking carefully about ideas for weeks now. I hope this idea is interesting to readers, or more accurately, that it can become interesting.

item.title: Re: JANUARY 2021 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Hello hello DrTarin! Welcome to the Wiki! I'm Ralliston, a site author and a member of the Community Outreach Team - with this helpful little comment, I'll try to help you find your way around the site and link a bunch of useful places and links that will help you in your SCP journey.

It's great to see that after all of these years, you finally decided to make an account on-site. After all, that's the only way you can contribute - speaking of which, it's also awesome to see you want to be a site author too! Don't worry, I'm sure that during your stay here you definitely will gain some knowledge regarding how to write things the site likes and how to write stuff you are happy with, too!

Without further ado though, let's click this collapsible, shall we? :)

+ show block
– hide block

If you're going to try your hand at writing, try out our Sandbox. You can make yourself a page here to store your drafts, which are in-works articles. Using it, you can link the drafts to reviewers to get their opinions on them before posting. It really helps everyone out a lot.

For brainstorming concepts, try out the Ideas and Brainstorming forum. You can run your ideas by experienced members of the community if you need help refining and fleshing out your concept. It's a very helpful little place for when you want to start your writing journey, especially when you're not sure if the idea is all that great.

If you have a draft ready, make a thread in the Drafts and Critiques forum. Remember to check the stickied posts in the relevant thread for guidelines on how best to use each forum. You can also try the IRC chat for real-time feedback.

From site usage to writing tips, the Guide Hub contains a wealth of resources geared towards helping members produce successful articles. Within the Guides, you will find useful information written by experienced members of the site for the use of newer ones.

The more time you take to familiarize yourself with the SCP style, the drafting process, and the community, the greater your chances are for success! Remember - there is no rush to writing - take your time! The more time you spend on fleshing your ideas out, the more your chance of success becomes!

As far as reading is concerned, you might want to check out Top Rated New Pages, which will display the most popular recent articles. It's helpful to keep up with what's being received well by the community to implement into your very own writing. Alternatively, you might want to look at the User Curated Lists page, where members of the community list and rank their favorite articles in different genres and themes, showing which attempts at such are successful and what the community likes.

Best of luck with your future contributions to the site! I hope you enjoy your time here as much as we do! If you have any more questions, feel free to message me here on Wikidot or on the IRC chats!

item.title: The Artifact - SCP Concept
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Horror

Page Layout: Apart from the standard description and containment procedures, there will be a log of the containment breach of the anomaly following an agent attempting to survive and escape.

Elevator Pitch: It will be an anomalous disease that causes every infected organism to become a "low poly model" of themselves, their "textures" to have JPEG artifacts, and their voice to have compression artifacts. Additionally, the infected individual is perceived like a bad CGI, staying at the same place relative to the observer's eyes. The disease is spread through touch or prolonged exposure.

Central Narrative: The main part will be the log of the Site-195 containment breach, following an agent attempting to first contain the SCP, and then escape the site. The log will be accompanied by several pictures, and audio and video recordings from the agent's camera. The story itself will be about the agent. At first, they and their fellow agents will try to contain the breach, but as the site gets more and more overrun, it soon become obvious that they'll fail. The agent gets in contact with an off site administrator, asking what to do, and they decide that they will detonate the site self destruct mechanism, as the site is built only to contain this specific anomaly. But before the detonation, the administrator requires more data in case there will be another outbreak, so the agent grabs recording equipment and starts following the administrator's tasks until they'll let them run away. In the end, the administrator decides that it's too much of a risk to let the agent out, as he might already be infected, and detonates the self destruct mechanism with the agent still inside.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The main attention grabber is the log. Two parts of the log are attention grabs. First is the story, which will be a suspence story. The other is the media captured from the agent's recording equipment.

Additional Notes: I mainly want feedback on the idea, as I believe in my ability to create low poly 3d models and put them on pictures, and in audio editing.

item.title: Re: Semi-Veil breaking Parawatch SCP idea
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for crit
– hide block

however the member believes that all anomalies should be known to the public, which is why they joined Parawatch.

This motivation feels a lot more Serpents Hand-y than it does Parawatch-y; I don't think this is a huge concern but it might be worth thinking about.

My core concern is that this still feels extremely focussed on the Parawatch poster: I don't think this is necessarily a bad idea but it feels like everything is being driven by what they do and how they feel about the situation and it feels to me like this will be really hard for you to convey via the framing of a SCP article, where you can't like, directly get into their head or anything.

My other concern is there's a feeling of this lacking stakes: like it's obviously bad if Parawatch has all this information, and the foundation trying to shut down parawatch isn't a bad response or anything; but it feels like there's not really a sense of 'if parawatch does x, y will happen; so we have to prevent x'. On the flip side, there's not really a sense of the Foundation's actions having consequences either: like, if the Foundation does shut this down, what happens?

Iunno, really what I'm getting at is there's a lot of this I kinda like but it feels like it's missing something to just, really get it to work and I'm not quite sure what it is. It might be just some emotional framing: like, who are we rooting for here? What point are you making about releasing information about all anomalies to the public?

item.title: EAS Alerts that predict disaster.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes.

PageType: Scp Article.

ElevatorPitch: There is a radio station at a undisclosed location within North America that when active sends out a broadcast bi-monthly of upcoming events, most frequently natural disasters before they occur.However on rare occasions it will send out a alert for an upcoming Scp or containment breach.It will state the day and area it will occur in and what protocols to take in order to survive or even recontain if possible.

CentralNarrative: The Foundation goes through a ethical dilemma of sort over whether or not to trust the information given by the alerts.However when the information provided proves to be correct and vital for minimizing casualties they slowly begin to trust and utilize it.The advice for recontainment is in particular valuable for Scps whose properties are not yet fully understood.

Hook: It will be revealed later after discovering the origins of this anomaly to be that of the chaos insurgency however that it wasn’t predicting these events, it was causing them and by keeping the signal active in order to save lives they have accidentally killed quite a few people.It’s true nature in essence is that it’s warnings are a self fulfilling prophecy.

item.title: Re: SCP: The Crusader Pond
item.content:encoded:
Thank you for responding, I was thinking about this idea for a while and thinking what I can do to revise this and I’m glad you pointed out the questions that were unanswered so I can development to this idea.

So to sum it up:

+ show block
– hide block

1. The pond is the reason how the Templar Knight statues form. And for the historical stuff, I originally was thinking about having the location being in Russia due to the fact that the Crusades took place in Europe but I didn’t know too much about the SCP lore with Russia other than it existed due to SCP-610 but I do think the location of the SCP needs a revision on it to make sense since iirc, I don’t think the Crusades have history to the land that was going to be known as Alaska years later.

2. I wanted to say no when reading this question first and say that it’s the statues that is causing them. However, I felt that (and possibly you agree here) that this feels cliché to leave it on a “it’s unknown what causes them” thing and not have an implication of it. So I’d imagine that it has something to do with either the souls of the Knights or God itself influencing them.

3. Well, if we go back the history of the Templar Knights, they were believers of Christianity and the idea I was going for was that the Templar Knights would be against the SCP Foundation due to their cold way of doing their experiments as I’d imagine, to some religious people, that containing SCPs would be something God would be against (this is not a representation of religious people, this is just an example of how this might make sense).

Hopefully this clears a lot of things up with the idea and hopefully I can do more revisions on this idea!

item.title: Re: The Screen Crawler
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for crit
– hide block

At the same time researches experimented with the SCP and discover its intellect and decide to allow interaction between SCP-079 and this SCP(SCP-5645).

this is a bad idea; having interactions between anomalies when you don't know what happens is a great way to have something really bad happen; and indeed, your entire narrative here is an example of why this is like, a bad idea.

Beyond this, my core concern is that like…none of this feels particularly interesting. It feels like it's just an extremely generic containment breach story which doesn't really explore why 5645 is interesting on it's own or really do anything further with it's properties beyond the way it causes a breach; and I'm just left not feeling like I like any part of this concept.

Part of this is the idea itself: the core anomaly still feels way too overcomplex for my liking. I generally think that having an anomaly with a single, relatively easy to explain anomalous property is the way to go; and having to just, elide all the abilities cos there's too many to mention is not something I'm particularly interested in; especially when they're all vaguely 'can interact with electronics' in nature.

Part of this is the narrative: none of it really goes anywhere? There's a whole interaction with 079 but it kinda fizzles out (see '079 eventually forgets about the situation') rather than being a big climactic thing; and without this, there's just…vague containment breach and temporary 079 shutdown to pretend it's dead and I'm not that into it as a narrative.

My advice to you is to like…take it slow; read a bunch of the writing guides in the comprehensive guide hub, read a bunch of modern SCPs and come back to this when you've really got a better idea of how SCPs tell stories.

item.title: Re: SCP Idea - Laptop with the ability of abduction
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for crit

I like the idea of the setting of this, that is: I like the core anomaly and I like what the anomaly does; and the implied emotional reaction to that which occurs.

There's two things that feel a little off to me: the self-healing exterior and the compelling of the viewer to click the video. The first feels like the kinda detail you add to explain why the laptop hasn't been destroyed and it feels unnecessary to me because like, the foundation doesn't destroy things. The second feels unnecessary because like, the thumbnails already act as a lure to tempt people into clicking and it's a lot more interesting if someone chooses to click despite the danger than if they're forced to click despite the danger.

My, central issue is of specifics: you've told us in general what the SCP can do but I want to know specifically what you want to do with the SCP: how are you having people be affected by this? How are you conveying the like, horror of not knowing whether the person in the video is alive or dead but believing them to be in extreme pain? Really these questions can be summarised as 'what are you actually intending to put in the article to show the horror/mystery of this?'.

item.title: Re: SCP DnD campaign
item.content:encoded:
Honestly I can only think of one problem. If you are setting a DnD campaign about SCP's you gotta think it through. So here are some questions I would ask myself if I would make this sort of thing.

What map will you play on?

Honestly I would play on site-11 since it is a complex "housing district" but site-19 works well.

What SCP's do you think you need to add? And who should they be fighting?

First of all as Kothardarastrix stated, it would be better if who you'd play as were G.O.C agents and operatives since they want to kill SCP's. And second you need SCP's that are killable so no SCP-682 or SCP-096 and many more that are un-reachable and are unkillable. Unless you wish to use Thaumiel or helpful SCP's in your party that can kill them. But I doubt any friendly and helpful SCP's will be able to kill these monsters

What will be the campaign's goal?

Well if you plan on using G.O.C obviously to kill every SCP that you can kill.
If you plan on using Chaos Insurgency well use SCP's to make the foundation's life living hell. Read about other GOI's since there are a lot of them and you got a pretty good story.

Can i use other GOI's? like chaos insurgency or the the church of the second hytoth?

item.title: Re: Robot Refugees From Outer Space
item.content:encoded:
Hello Dootboy96! let's take a look :)

SAND

+ show block
– hide block

The concept:

Elevator Pitch: Three extraterrestrial lifeforms mechanical in nature claiming to be millions of years old and a machine they refer to as "The Forge" have been recently detained. Apparently they are the last remaining members of their species, and the Forge is their last hope of saving it. The Forge is a highly advanced piece of technology that is the robots' main method of reproduction, able to practically 3D print new members of their species under the correct circumstances. According to the three, Earth has the perfect conditions to incubate the Forge. However, the Forge supplies itself with the materials necessary to undergo such processes by absorbing and thaumaturgically converting large amounts of matter. Due to the catastrophic implications of letting a machine like this function on Earth, consuming the world's resources, the Foundation has concluded that the Forge must be destroyed ASAP before a GH-O 'Dead Greenhouse' Scenario could occur. There is only one problem, though: the Forge is nigh-indestructible by conventional means. But the Foundation is quickly looking into ways of solving this problem.

My main issue here is the Foundations motive to have the machine destroyed, while using it does pose a threat to life on earth, there isn't really any clear indications that the skips were going to use it no-matter what (in fact they sounds very civil). Considering there isn't a clear danger to keeping it around, it sounds more plausible that it would just be kept in containment. -The Foundation would only really destroy something if they absolutely had too, considering the skips sound reasonable/negotiable its odd they would be so set on destroying it.

Along with this, I feel the skips themselves aren't really expanded on or explained much. Currently, they're only really shown fighting off the Foundation? which (to me) makes the narrative feel a bit flat, along with making the 'aliens' themselves feel a bit cliched.- Currently nothing really separates them from the "they're going to invade us" trope.

The narrative:

Central Narrative: The three aliens learn they must race against the clock to breach containment, secure the Forge, and escape the Foundation before the machine is destroyed, sealing their species' fate for good. However, if they successfully incubate the Forge on Earth, it could very well mean the end of organic life as we know it.

As for the narrative, there isn't really enough of an arc here to get an idea of happens or how this would look in a draft. There doesn't seem to be much on where and how the skips were found, what actually takes place (there isn't really a clear progression here?), and what everything is building up to.

In general, I would recommend developing the skips a little more. perhaps show a bit more their journey across space, why and how they found earth and what the consequence of them not operating here would be. Allow the audience to get a feel for what and who they are, rather than just painting them as what essentially boils down to "aliens that are trying to invade earth".

- perhaps this could work a bit better if the conflict was more focused on the Foundations containment than anything? maybe they only want to leave in search of an easier place to populate, but the Foundation refuses, or is very reluctant to let them leave?

Red or green?
Due to my afore mentioned concerns, no-greenlight.

If you would like me review this (or any concept) further, then please feel free to send me a PM or ask via IRC. Response times generally range from 2-12 hours over PMs. If your looking for additional critiques/perspectives in general, then I would highly recommend contacting the butterfly squad :)

Cheers,
